terms.comment: Classically talk or conversation; Augustine’s word for his sermons to the people. To preach a sermon is sermōnem ad populum habēre (Egger, in Morgan–Owens).
Greek ὁμιλία, a talk; the usual word for a sermon that explains the day’s Gospel.

sources: Lewis & Short: sermo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 376, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. preach: sermon.
Homīlia is not in Lewis & Short; its quantities are Traupman’s.
